newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dubinin says Russia has reserves to defend rouble.
newsitem.headline: Dubinin says Russia has reserves to defend rouble.

text.p: Central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Wednesday that Russia has sufficient reserves to keep the rouble within its exchange rate corridor against the dollar.

Dubinin told a news conference Russia had, in spite of significant intervention to support the rouble in August, managed to keep its foreign reserves within levels agreed with the International Monetary Fund.

"Despite the quite large volume of intervention, by buying gold and other similar operations, we are managing to support the necessary level of net international reserves and not to allowing a fall either in gross or net reserves," he said.
Dubinin earlier said the bank had spent $1.6 billion on intervention in August, when a faster than usual decline in the rouble made short-term T-bills unattractive.
Under Russia's crawling peg exchange rate policy, which runs until the end of this year, the rouble should be trading in a 5,500-6,100 per dollar corridor on December 31 this year.
The rouble was fixed at 5,373 per dollar on Wednesday on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX).

"We have sufficient reserves to keep the rouble exchange rate within the framework of the corridor as we consider necessary," said Dubinin, adding they were approximately the same as at the beginning of July.
He said in late July that gross central bank reserves in mid-July were $14.9 billion.
Net reserves are one of the economic indicators for which the IMF has set targets under its $10 billion, three-year loan agreement with Russia.
First deputy chairman Alexander Khandruyev said the current situation was calm, but that there was some pressure on the rouble.
He said the bank's board had on Wednesday discussed various options for exchange rate policy after the expiry of the corridor. It was not yet clear which would be adopted.
